alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The ciliary body is the anterior expansion of the choroid, forming a ring encircling the lens. When cut in cross section, the ciliary body appears triangular in shape. The ciliary body contains the ciliary muscle, three subdivisions of smooth muscle that alter the shape of the lens via suspensory fibers that extend between the ciliary body and the lens.

alternativas.feedback: The trabecular meshwork, located in the limbus, is a series of endothelium-lined channels that drain aqueous humor from the anterior chamber of the eye. Aqueous humor flows from the trabecular meshwork into the larger canal of Schlemm, which connects with the venous system external to the eye.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The cornea, located in the anterior one-fifth of the eye, is the transparent portion of the outer tunic, where major refraction occurs. Its convex curvature aids in focusing light. The cornea consists of inner and outer epithelial layers that sandwich a stroma of collagen fibers that are precisely aligned to provide transparency to the cornea. The cornea is surfaced by the corneal epithelium that transitions to the bulbar conjunctiva that covers the sclera.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The anterior chamber is bounded by the cornea, iris and anterior surface of the lens. The chamber is filled with aqueous humor, a watery fluid produced by the ciliary body. Aqueous humor flows through the posterior chamber into the anterior chamber and exits at the limbus via the trabecular meshwork and the canal of Schlemm.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The choroid forms the majority of the vascular or middle tunic (uvea), covering the posterior portion of the eye. The choroid is composed of loose connective tissue, with an abundant vascular supply and pigmented cells. The choroid supplies nutrients to the deep layers of the retina; its pigmented cells serve to absorb reflected and stray light within the globe.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The sclera, a component of the fibrous tunic, is an opaque layer surrounding the posterior four-fifths of the eye. The sclera is composed of dense connective tissue that provides support for the eye and attachment for extraocular eye muscles.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The ciliary muscle, located within the ciliary body, is composed of smooth muscle fibers oriented in three planes. The fibers insert onto the sclera and ciliary body and contraction releases tension on the zonule fibers, allowing the lens to become more spherical during the process of accommodation.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The ciliary processes are ridge-like extensions of the ciliary body and are also covered by ciliary epithelium. Zonular fibers are delicate microfibrils that arise from the basal lamina of the ciliary epithelium in the grooves separating the ciliary processes. Zonular fibers attach to the lens capsule and contraction of ciliary body muscles alters the tension on these fibers and, thus, affects the shape of the lens.

alternativas.feedback: The iris is a portion of the middle, or vascular, tunic and is attached to the anterior portion of the ciliary body. The iris is a disk-shaped structure with a central opening, the pupil. Most of the core of the iris consists of loose connective tissue with many melanocytes and blood vessels. Contraction of smooth muscle groups in the iris alters the diameter of the pupil and, therefore, adjust the amount of light entering the eye.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Pigment epithelium constitutes the outermost layer of the retina and consists of a simple cuboidal epithelium with melanin granules. Pigment epithelial cells phagocytose worn-out components of photoreceptors, absorb light passing through the retina to prevent reflection, and form the blood-retinal barrier. The basal lamina of this epithelium is a component of Bruch's membrane.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Cones are less numerous than rods and provide greater visual acuity than the rods. Cones are so named based of the conical shape of their outer segments which contain the visual pigment iodopsin. Cones are concentrated in the central retina, notably in the fovea, the region of greatest visual acuity.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The outer limiting membrane is not a true membrane. It is formed by adherent junctions between Muller cells, radially oriented astrocytes, and with the photoreceptors. Muller cells extend between the outer and inner limiting membranes and support and nourish the retinal neurons and their processes.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The orbicularis oculi muscle is skeletal muscle, a portion of which is located in the core of the eyelid. The orbicularis oculi muscle is a sphincter muscle that closes the eyelids. Also present in the eyelid are Meibomian glands, modified sebaceous glands, embedded in the tarsus. The secretions of these glands provide an oily surface layer to the tear film that reduces evaporation of this layer.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The fovea is the region of the retina providing greatest visual acuity. It consists entirely of cones; other retinal layers are displaced centrifugally to create an unimpeded path for light to reach the photoreceptors. The center of the fovea is called the foveola.
